documents.title: Intimation Of Book Closure - Pursuant To Regulation 42 Of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015.
Intimation Of 34Th Annual General Meeting To Be Held On Tuesday, September 29, 2026 And Book Closure.

analysis.summary: California Software Company Limited issued its Annual Report for the financial year 2025-26 along with the notice for its 34th Annual General Meeting scheduled for September 29, 2026. The document details resolutions concerning the adoption of financial statements, the retirement of a director by rotation, and the re-appointment of independent and whole-time directors. Additionally, it outlines procedures for electronic voting, video conferencing attendance, and statutory compliances. Management focused their annual report on empowering small and microbusinesses through artificial intelligence (AI) during the fiscal year 2024-25. The company invested in AI-driven platforms such as dSpeedUp, dRyZe CRM, dBotMinds, and Zaywoo to democratize advanced technology and help small enterprises compete globally.

orders_capacity.claim: dSpeedUp's digital ecosystem grew to serve over 1000 merchants, achieving 95% annual client retention.
orders_capacity.quote: dSpeedUp’s digital ecosystem grew to serve over 1000 merchants, achieving 95% annual client retention as small retailers and service providers embraced the platform’s benefits..

capital_allocation.claim: The company stated that the transfer of unclaimed dividend amounts and shares to the IEPF account and Demat account of the IEPF Authority does not arise as no dividend was declared for the year 2015-16.
capital_allocation.quote: As the Company has not declared any dividend for the year 2015-16, the transfer of the amount of dividend that remains unclaimed for a period of 7 years to the IEPF account and the shares on which dividends remain unpaid or unclaimed for a period of seven consecutive years or more to the Demat account of IEPF Authority does not arise;

management_commitments.claim: Calsoft's mission in FY 2024-25 centered on democratizing advanced technology for startups, retailers, local service providers, and microentrepreneurs.
management_commitments.quote: Calsoft’s mission in FY 2024–25 centered on democratizing advanced technology for the “fortune five million” – the startups, mom-and-pop retailers, local service providers, and microentrepreneurs that form the backbone of the economy.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
